# Appendix A: Ubuntu-to-Other Platforms Mapping

This appendix maps **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS** operational patterns used in this book to common alternatives. Prefer the Ubuntu column as the reference implementation; use others only when portability requires it.

## Package management

| Task | Ubuntu 24.04 | Debian | RHEL / Rocky / Alma | Arch | Alpine |
|------|--------------|--------|---------------------|------|--------|
| Update index | `apt update` | `apt update` | `dnf check-update` | `pacman -Sy` | `apk update` |
| Upgrade | `apt full-upgrade` | same | `dnf upgrade` | `pacman -Syu` | `apk upgrade` |
| Install | `apt install pkg` | same | `dnf install pkg` | `pacman -S pkg` | `apk add pkg` |
| Remove purge | `apt autoremove --purge` | same | `dnf remove` | `pacman -Rns` | `apk del` |
| Auto security | `unattended-upgrades` | same | `dnf-automatic` | custom/timers | custom |
| Query file owner | `dpkg -S /path` | same | `rpm -qf /path` | `pacman -Qo` | `apk info -W` |

## Network configuration

| Task | Ubuntu (netplan) | RHEL-like | Traditional Debian | Notes |
|------|------------------|-----------|--------------------|-------|
| Primary tool | `netplan` YAML → networkd/NM | NetworkManager `nmcli` | `/etc/network/interfaces` or NM | Book standard: netplan |
| Apply | `netplan try` / `netplan apply` | `nmcli con up` | `ifreload -a` | Prefer safe try on remote |
| Config path | `/etc/netplan/*.yaml` | `/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/` | `/etc/network/interfaces.d/` | |
| DNS status | `resolvectl` | `resolvectl` / `nmcli` | varies | systemd-resolved common |
| Show routes | `ip route` | same | same | Portable |
| WireGuard | `wg-quick@wg0` | same packages | same | Portable userspace/tools |

### netplan → NetworkManager intent example

Ubuntu static:

```yaml
addresses: [10.20.30.10/24]
routes: [{to: default, via: 10.20.30.1}]
nameservers: {addresses: [10.20.30.1]}
```

nmcli sketch:

```bash
nmcli con add type ethernet ifname eth0 con-name static \
  ipv4.method manual ipv4.addresses 10.20.30.10/24 \
  ipv4.gateway 10.20.30.1 ipv4.dns 10.20.30.1
```

## Service management

| Task | Ubuntu systemd | Notes on non-systemd |
|------|----------------|----------------------|
| Start/enable | `systemctl enable --now foo` | OpenRC: `rc-update add`; runit: different |
| Status | `systemctl status foo` | |
| Logs | `journalctl -u foo -f` | file logs under `/var/log` if no journal |
| Reload units | `systemctl daemon-reload` | |
| Timers | `systemctl list-timers` | cron remains universal fallback |
| User services | `systemctl --user` | |

This book assumes **systemd** on server Ubuntu. Containers may use a minimal init—manage the app with the container runtime instead.

## Firewall and filtering

| Task | Ubuntu | RHEL-like | Cloud |
|------|--------|-----------|-------|
| Host FW UX | `ufw` | `firewall-cmd` | + provider NSG/security groups |
| Backend | nftables (via ufw) | firewalld → nft/iptables | |
| Allow SSH | `ufw allow OpenSSH` | `firewall-cmd --add-service=ssh` | open port 22 carefully |
| Default deny in | `ufw default deny incoming` | zone policies | deny + explicit allows |

Always combine **guest firewall** with **provider perimeter** (Azure NSG, home router).

## Logging and time

| Task | Ubuntu 24.04 | Portable alternative |
|------|--------------|----------------------|
| System logs | `journalctl` | `/var/log/syslog` if rsyslog installed |
| Time sync | `systemd-timesyncd` / chrony | `chronyd` everywhere is fine |
| Timezone | `timedatectl set-timezone` | same on systemd distros |
| NTP check | `timedatectl status` | `chronyc tracking` |

## Identity and SSH

| Task | Ubuntu | Universal |
|------|--------|-----------|
| sshd config drop-in | `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf` | same on modern OpenSSH |
| Reload ssh | `systemctl reload ssh` | service name may be `sshd` |
| sudoers | `/etc/sudoers.d/` via `visudo` | same |
| fail2ban | `apt install fail2ban` | package name usually same |

On RHEL, the unit is often `sshd` not `ssh`.

## Cloud-init and first boot

| Platform | Mechanism |
|----------|-----------|
| Ubuntu cloud images | cloud-init (reference) |
| Proxmox | cloud-init drive + snippets |
| Azure | custom data / extensions + waagent |
| AWS | user-data cloud-init |
| GCP | startup scripts / cloud-init |

Keep **user-data YAML** portable; avoid vendor-only keys when possible.

## Hypervisor / hosting map

| Concern | Proxmox VE | Azure VM | Other VPS |
|---------|------------|----------|-----------|
| Guest OS focus | Ubuntu VM | Ubuntu VM | Ubuntu VM |
| Templates | QM template | Image Gallery | Snapshots/images |
| Snapshots | qemu/ZFS/LVM | Managed disk snapshots | provider dependent |
| Guest agent | qemu-guest-agent | Azure Linux Agent | qemu/VMware tools |
| Backup | vzdump + guest restic | Azure Backup + restic | provider + restic |

## Container runtimes

| Task | Docker (Ubuntu) | Podman | Kubernetes |
|------|-----------------|--------|------------|
| Run | `docker run` / compose | `podman` / quadlet | manifests/helm |
| Boot integrate | compose + restart policy | systemd quadlets | deployments |
| Rootless | possible | default emphasis | varies |

Book default: containers **inside** Ubuntu VMs, not on Proxmox host.

## Quick translation cheat sheet

```text
apt install X          → dnf install X
systemctl reload ssh   → systemctl reload sshd
ufw allow 443          → firewall-cmd --add-port=443/tcp --permanent && firewall-cmd --reload
netplan apply          → nmcli con up <name>
journalctl -u foo      → (same on systemd) or tail -f /var/log/foo.log
```

## How to use this appendix

1. Implement on Ubuntu 24.04 first (main chapters).  
2. When porting, translate **intent** (deny inbound, static IP, auto security updates), not only commands.  
3. Record deviations in ADRs and service blueprints.  

## Path and config file map

| Concern | Ubuntu 24.04 path | Notes elsewhere |
|---------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Netplan | `/etc/netplan/*.yaml` | NM keyfiles; `interfaces` |
| systemd units | `/etc/systemd/system/` | same on systemd distros |
| sshd drop-ins | `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/` | same modern OpenSSH |
| UFW rules | `/etc/ufw/` | firewalld zones |
| apt sources | `/etc/apt/` | `/etc/yum.repos.d/` |
| cloud-init | `/etc/cloud/`, `/var/lib/cloud/` | often similar |
| persistent journals | `/var/log/journal/` | optional |
| WireGuard | `/etc/wireguard/` | same |
| Let’s Encrypt | `/etc/letsencrypt/` | certbot layout common |
| Caddy data | `/var/lib/caddy/` | if used |
| Homelab secrets (book) | `/etc/homelab/secrets/` | convention, not OS |
| Service data (book) | `/srv/<service>/` | convention |

## Proxmox host vs Ubuntu guest

Do **not** conflate these operating planes:

| Plane | OS | You manage |
|-------|-----|------------|
| Hypervisor | Proxmox (Debian-based) | storage, VMs, bridges, vzdump |
| Guest | Ubuntu 24.04 | netplan, apt, systemd apps |
| Cloud control | Azure ARM | RG, NSG, disks, RBAC |
| Cloud guest | Ubuntu 24.04 | same as edge guest |

Book automation targets **guests** first. Hypervisor and cloud control plane stay thin and documented separately.

## When *not* to multi-home the same runbook

If a command depends on `apt`, `netplan`, or `ufw`, keep a **Ubuntu runbook** and a short “portability delta” rather than one mega-script full of conditionals. Conditionals hide drift; deltas teach.
